body.x: Meta Heart Inc. (CEO Kimoo Lim) will exhibit at the K-Startup Pavilion at CES 2025, which will take place from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. Founded in September 2022, the company aims to commercialize in silico biological modeling software for research and education, leveraging two decades of academic expertise in computer-based biological modeling.

Meta Heart specializes in advanced AI and silico biological modeling. It develops software such as CardioSim and ToxCML for drug toxicity evaluation and CVS-Twin for cardiovascular digital twin technology. These innovations improve safety and efficiency in drug development while introducing new approaches to cardiovascular disease management.

Meta Heart has received government support, including funding from the Pre-Startup and Early-Stage Startup Packages, which has enabled the completion of its flagship product, CardioSim. Currently in beta testing at Korea's Safety Assessment Research Institute, the software integrates in vitro cardiac toxicity evaluation systems with Meta Heart’s in silico solutions, aligning with FDA ICH protocols. Following regulatory updates from Korea’s Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, Meta Heart plans to market the product to pharmaceutical companies and research institutes.

CardioSim, to be showcased at CES 2025, meets the latest guidelines of the International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH). The in silico heart model-based toxicity assessment system reduces time and costs in evaluating a drug's cardiac impact. The software leverages computer simulations and AI to predict arrhythmia risks and systematically assesses the electrophysiological properties of heart cells.

By integrating multi-ion channel in vitro test data with in silico heart models, CardioSim enables precise predictions of a drug's effects on cardiac cells, enhancing the accuracy of cardiac toxicity risk assessments. This aligns with the Comprehensive in vitro Proarrhythmia Assay (CiPA) guidelines, which aim to minimize the risks of cardiac-related adverse effects during drug development.

Meta Heart's representative noted that CardioSim adheres to regulatory requirements in the U.S., Europe, and Japan, where updated guidelines replace the traditional S7B and E14 cardiac toxicity assessment protocols. Korea is also revising its guidelines, positioning the company to target all markets governed by these regulations.

“All drug types and purposes require cardiac toxicity assessments, making the entire pharmaceutical market our target,” a Meta Heart representative explained. “The global pharmaceutical market exceeds $1 trillion, with 4–7% annual growth rates. Korea’s market alone is worth over 23 trillion KRW, representing 1.6% of the global market. Considering ongoing drug development, we anticipate multi-million-dollar revenue potential.”

Meta Heart’s participation in CES 2025 seeks to establish its groundbreaking technology as a standard for drug toxicity assessment, fostering opportunities for collaboration and global market expansion.
